          Pursuant to Section 203(a)(1) of the Federal Power Act, as amended (“FPA”), 1 and Part 33

of the Rules and Regulations of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or the

“Commission”), 2 Viridon Wisconsin LLC (“VWI”) and NGV US Transmission Inc. (“Buyer”)

(collectively, the “Applicants”) respectfully submit this application (“Application”) requesting all

authorizations necessary for the proposed transaction that would result in a change in upstream

ownership of VWI through the sale by Viridon Midcontinent LLC (“VMC” or “Seller”) of 50%

of the limited liability company interests in Viridon Wisconsin Holdings LLC (“VWI Holdings”),

VWI’s indirect upstream owner, to Buyer (the “Proposed Transaction”).

          As demonstrated in Section II below, the Proposed Transaction will not have an adverse

effect on competition, rates, or regulation, and will not result in any cross-subsidization of an

affiliate or the encumbrance or pledge of utility assets for the benefit of an associate company. The

Commission should therefore authorize the Proposed Transaction pursuant to Section 203 of the

FPA as consistent with the public interest without hearing or condition.

 II.       THE PROPOSED TRANSACTION IS CONSISTENT WITH THE PUBLIC
          INTEREST.

          The Commission is required to authorize a transaction pursuant to Section 203(a)(4) of the

FPA “if it finds that the proposed transaction will be consistent with the public interest, and will

not result in cross-subsidization of a non-utility associate company or the pledge or encumbrance

of utility assets for the benefit of an associate company.” 16 FERC considers three primary factors

in determining whether a transaction is in the public interest: (1) the effect on competition; (2) the

effect on rates; and (3) the effect on regulation. 17 As explained below, the Proposed Transaction

will not have any adverse effect on competition, rates, or regulation, and will not cause cross-

subsidization or the pledge or encumbrance of utility assets at the time of the completion of the

Proposed Transaction or in the future. Accordingly, the Commission should promptly find that the

Proposed Transaction is consistent with the public interest and authorize the Proposed Transaction.

          A.       The Proposed Transaction Will Have No Adverse Effect on Competition.

          When considering impacts on competition, the Commission reviews both horizontal

market power effects that may result from any increases in concentration in energy and capacity

markets and vertical market power effects that may result from increases in the ability or incentive

to leverage control over electric transmission or natural gas transportation facilities or other inputs

to electric generation in order to enhance revenues in generation markets. 18 As discussed in more

detail below, the Proposed Transaction does not raise any competitive issues.

                   1.          The Proposed Transaction Does Not Raise Horizontal Market Power
                              Concerns.

         Section 33.3(a)(1) of the Commission’s regulations requires a horizontal competitive

analysis “if, as a result of the proposed transaction, a single corporate entity obtains ownership or

control over the generating facilities of previously unaffiliated merging entities.” 19 As described

above, the Proposed Transaction does not involve the change in ownership or control of any

generation assets or jurisdictional facilities used for wholesale power sales. Rather, the Proposed

Transaction only involves the indirect change in upstream ownership of VWI’s transmission

formula rate. 20 In Order No. 642, the Commission recognized that a transfer that involves only

transmission facilities does not raise the same types of concerns about horizontal market power

and exempted such applicants from having to provide the horizontal competitive screen analysis. 21

         Here, the Proposed Transaction will have no effect on the market share or competitive

position of the VWI, and it will have no impact on the competitive situation in any market.

Accordingly, consistent with precedent, the Commission should conclude that the Proposed

Transaction does not raise horizontal market power concerns.

                  2.          The Proposed Transaction Does Not Raise Vertical Market Power
                              Concerns.

         After consummation of the Proposed Transaction, VWI will continue to pursue

development, ownership, and operation of transmission projects in the MISO region. Any

transmission facilities developed by VWI will be turned over to the operational control of MISO,

which will provide services pursuant to MISO’s Commission-approved OATT. Accordingly, the

Proposed Transaction raises no vertical market power concerns because transmission facilities

          D.      The Proposed Transaction Will Not Result in Improper Cross-Subsidization
                 or the Pledge or Encumbrance of Utility Assets.

         Pursuant to Section 203(a)(4) of the FPA and Section 33.2(j) of the Commission’s

regulations, FERC evaluates whether a proposed transaction will result in the cross-subsidization

of a non-utility associate company or the pledge or encumbrance of utility assets for the benefit of

an associate company. In Order Nos. 669, 669-A, and 669-B, 28 the Commission established a four-

part test that FPA Section 203 applicants must satisfy in order to demonstrate that a transaction

will not result in improper cross-subsidization, or the pledge or encumbrance of utility assets of a

traditional public utility associate company that has captive customers or that owns or provides

transmission service over jurisdictional transmission facilities. Under this test, the Commission

examines whether, at the time of the transaction or in the future, the transaction will result in:

         (i)     any transfer of facilities between a traditional public utility associate company that
                 has captive customers or that owns or provides transmission service over
                 jurisdictional transmission facilities, and an associate company;

         (ii)    any new issuance of securities by a traditional public utility associate company that
                 has captive customers or that owns or provides transmission service over
                 jurisdictional transmission facilities, for the benefit of an associate company;

         (iii)   any pledge or encumbrance of assets of traditional public utility associate company
                 that has captive customers or that owns or provides transmission service over
                 jurisdictional transmission facilities, for the benefit of an associate company; or

         (iv)    any new affiliate contract between a non-utility associate company and a traditional
                 public utility associate company that has captive customers or that owns or provides
                 transmission service over jurisdictional transmission facilities, other than non-
                 power goods and services agreements subject to review under Sections 205 and 206
                 of the FPA. 29

utility. None of the Buyer’s traditional public utility affiliates are involved in the Proposed
